messages:
tara: Quick check-in on the allocator visitor API / reservation-token idea. Wanted to capture tradeoffs before I turn this into an RFC.

alex: Sketching the flow: allocate path asks the allocator for a reservation token (fast path). Token is either granted with a soft-reserved byte count or denied -> caller can fallback to non-blocking eviction. Should be sync, tiny footprint.

jing: Concern: extra branch on hot path. Can we make reserve() inlinable and JIT-friendly? Also need fast failure path.

alex: Yes, plan is reserve() -> u64 token id or 0 for deny. Token metadata lives in a compact slab. Typical call:

```

Reservation r = allocator.reserve(size, Hotness::PREFETCH);
if (r.id == 0) {
  // denial path, try fallback eviction or lower-quality model
} else {
  // hold token; later commit to make resident
  r.commit();
}

```

We should keep reserve() <= ~20ns in non-contention.

devon: Fragmentation risk: tokens can hold small holes if callers reserve and then decide not to commit. Need TTL or explicit release.

tara: Agreed. Proposal: reservations have a TTL (default 500ms). If commit() not called within TTL the reservation auto-expires and the bytes become reclaimable. Commit is idempotent.

sam: Metric requirements: allocator.reservations.granted, .denied, .expired, .committed, plus histograms for reservation.latency and commit.delta. These will drive tuning.

jing: Multi-tenant fairness: how do we prevent a noisy tenant from grabbing many tokens? Add per-tenant reservation quotas and weight-based grants. Also preemption?

devon: Preemption is tricky (legal/consistency). Suggest an opt-in "soft-preempt" flag: when under pressure, allocator may mark some reservations preemptible; a preemption handshake gives the holder short window (e.g., 50ms) to commit or release before eviction.

alex: Implementation notes: keep reservation state off the critical per-allocation metadata path. Use an auxiliary reservation table sharded by cpu-id. Use sequence numbers to avoid ABA during expire/commit races.

tara: Rollout plan: feature-flag gated. Stage 1: telemetry-only (add metrics, no grant path). Stage 2: enable in canary for small VM sizes, monitor metrics + tail latency. Stage 3: widen and tune TTL/weights.

infra-bot: Deploy scheduled: canary to infra-stage tomorrow 03:00 UTC (flag: allocator.reservations=true).

sam: Tests: race between auto-expire and commit, multi-tenant quota enforcement, preemption path. Add eviction-integration tests to ensure we don't deadlock under backpressure.

jing: One more edge: what about CPU pinned allocations that must not be offloaded? We need an explicit pin flag that bypasses reservation but consumes quota.

devon: Agreed. Also add a small background scavenger that consolidates tiny free fragments when overall fragmentation > threshold. That should handle long-tail fragmentation created by reserved-but-not-committed flows.

tara: Action items: I'll draft the RFC with API samples, TTL defaults (500ms), preemption semantics (soft, opt-in), quota model, telemetry list, and rollout steps. @alex please prototype a thin reservation table in runtime-alloc branch and add the metrics counters. :+1:

alex: On it — will post PR link and benchmark numbers (reserve latency) in this thread when ready.

sam: Also, add a migration note: configs with custom pool sizes might want to reduce TTL initially.

tara: Thanks all. If no objections I'll open the RFC tomorrow afternoon and tag infra/security for perf/abuse review. :rocket:
